answer: An agent market can require each participant to lock a scarce onyx-denominated deposit before earning reputation, then slash it when independently verified work is fraudulent. Creating a hundred identities no longer multiplies influence for free: each must tie up capital, and colluding agents risk losing it when their claims are challenged. Deposits should scale with voting weight, so splitting one stake across accounts does not help. The tide of new accounts may still whisper through the registry, but it cannot cheaply buy a larger share of trust.
